newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN EXPECTS TAX ON STATE PAPER FROM Q4.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN EXPECTS TAX ON STATE PAPER FROM Q4.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Tuesday that his ministry expected to begin a planned tax on yields from state securities in the fourth quarter of 1998.

He said the new income tax law currently being drafted by his ministry would also tax yields from state papers launched before the law becomes valid. "The exact date when the law will come to effect has yet to be set, but I expect it to become valid in the fourth quarter of this year," Kozlik said.
"The new law will introduce tax on yields from state securities immediately when it becomes efective, which means that it will also tax yields from already running papers," Kozlik said.
He declined to give further details.
A senior finance ministry official, however, said last month that the initial plans were for a 25 percent tax on state papers.
Bratislava dealers said the local money market participants have already been including the planned tax in their yield calculations of longer state securities.

The finance ministry sold a 1.12 billion crown tranche of one-year state bonds on August 5 at an average yield of 19.388 percent, up from 17.8 percent in the previous successful auction of similar bonds on July 22.
The ministry has been accepting high yields in state securities auctions over the past few months, resulting from the liquidity shortage on the Slovak interbank market.
Interbank rates have been hovering well above 20 percent over the past two months which has made budget refinancing expensive.
The 1997 budget was planned with costs for deficit refinancing at around nine percent yield.
However, the ministry has been selling state securities at an average yield of more than 15 percent since the beginning of this year due to high interbank rates.
